strategy.thesis: Venture arm of the Cure Kids Foundation, New Zealand's largest private funder of child health research; invests in early-stage companies commercialising medical devices, medications, diagnostics, health information and care-delivery innovations with the potential to benefit child health, recycling returns back into child health research.

summary.en: Auckland-based venture-philanthropy fund owned by the Cure Kids Foundation, New Zealand's largest private funder of child health research; since 2008 it has built a ~17-company portfolio of early-stage medical device, diagnostics and digital-health ventures that benefit children's health.

strategy.thesis: Clinician-led angel syndicate of 1,000+ Australian medical practitioners (with reach into an extended ~40,000-clinician network) that evaluates and co-invests in early-stage healthcare startups spanning medical technology, digital health, medical devices and select life-science ventures; now backed by its own ESVCLP venture fund.

current_fund.raw: $40 million ESVCLP (Medical Angels Venture Fund I)

summary.en: Australia's leading medical-practitioner angel syndicate, uniting 1,000+ clinician investors to back early-stage healthtech, medtech and digital-health startups; co-founded by Dr Amandeep Hansra and Dr Mian Bi in 2019, it has since launched the $40M Medical Angels Venture Fund I (ESVCLP) and opened membership beyond clinicians to wholesale investors.

strategy.thesis: Dedicated health-technology and biotech investment vehicle of Tattarang, the private investment group of Andrew and Nicola Forrest; deployed as an evergreen, single-LP fund with no external investor or lender obligations, to back Australian health innovation in medical devices, diagnostics, pharmaceuticals and healthcare services, with stated interest in immunology, oncology, digital health, the microbiome and antimicrobial resistance, and an explicit focus on female-founded and female-led health businesses.

summary.en: Perth-headquartered, evergreen health-technology and biotech investment business of Tattarang, the Forrest family's private investment group; launched in 2022 with an initial $250M allocation, it invests without external LP obligations across immunology, oncology, digital health, the microbiome and antimicrobial resistance, with additional offices in Sydney and San Francisco.
